title: Idle session can be silently revived via refresh-token swap
description:
The server-side idle timeout (backend/app/auth/idle_session.py, wired via auth/service.py::enforce_idle_session) should 401 any request whose session has been inactive past settings.idle_timeout_seconds, forcing re-auth. Two independent bugs let an idle session silently re-arm itself.

Bug A — get_current_user_no_mfa skips the idle check entirely. It verifies the Firebase token and resolves the user but never calls idle_session.check_and_touch, so every endpoint depending on it (including GET /api/users/me/status, the SPA cold-load call) bypasses the idle gate. The _no_mfa dependency exists for pre-MFA-enrollment flows; the idle check only reads uid/auth_time and has no MFA dependency, so _no_mfa should not also mean _no_idle.

Bug B — 'marker missing' is conflated with 'first request of a new session'. check_and_touch has three branches: marker+activity present -> refresh activity; marker present, activity absent -> burn marker + 401 IDLE_TIMEOUT; marker absent -> seed both keys + allow (treated as fresh sign-in). The third branch cannot distinguish a brand-new sign-in from a marker that was burned minutes ago on idle-out. Refresh-token swaps reuse the same auth_time, so a previously-timed-out session resurrects on the next request from any other live session.

Fix:
- Bug A: call idle_session.check_and_touch(decoded_token) inside get_current_user_no_mfa, after verify_firebase_token and before _resolve_user. Use a lazy import, mirroring enforce_idle_session.
- Bug B: add a tombstone key idle:revoked:{uid}:{auth_time} with TTL = _SESSION_MARKER_TTL_SECONDS. Before the marker check, redis.exists(revoked_key) -> if present, raise 401 IDLE_TIMEOUT immediately without touching marker/activity. When the burn-marker branch fires, SET the tombstone in the same pipeline as the marker delete so both land atomically. Tombstone TTL matches marker TTL because the only way a timed-out auth_time returns is via the same refresh token, itself capped by Firebase's inactivity window.

Tests (backend/tests/test_idle_session.py):
1. Tombstone set on idle expiry — extend the burn-marker test to assert redis.exists(revoked key) and TTL ~ _SESSION_MARKER_TTL_SECONDS.
2. Tombstone short-circuits later requests — pre-seed the revoked key with no marker/activity, assert 401 IDLE_TIMEOUT and that marker/activity are NOT created (regression for Bug B).
3. No-MFA path enforces idle — call get_current_user_no_mfa with Redis state matching 'marker present, activity expired', assert 401 IDLE_TIMEOUT (regression for Bug A).

Acceptance: make check passes (lint + mypy + pytest); the three tests above are present and passing.
close_reason: merged

title: New-chat first message lost — panel remounts on lazy conversation create
description:
## Symptom (user-reproduced)

Open a new chat (click "New", or just start typing on a brand-new patient), type the FIRST message, submit → the chat window flashes "Loading conversation…", the message is LOST, and the panel resets. Typing again works. Intermittent-feeling but deterministic given the code path.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanelWithHistory.tsx:95` keys the ChatPanel on the conversation id:

    key={`${activeConversationId ?? "new"}::${panelMountId}`}

The first send lazily creates the conversation: `ChatPanel.performSend` calls `onConversationCreated(id)` (`ChatPanel.tsx:239`) BEFORE it runs `streamChatMessages` (`ChatPanel.tsx:257`). The parent handler then sets `activeConversationId = id` (`ChatPanelWithHistory.tsx:107`), which changes the key from `new::N` to `<id>::N`. React unmounts the in-flight panel and mounts a fresh one with `conversationId={id}` → `hydrating = Boolean(initialConversationId) = true` → renders "Loading conversation…" (`ChatPanel.tsx:445`) and runs the hydrate effect, which `getConversation`s the just-created, still-EMPTY conversation. The optimistic user/assistant bubbles and the SSE stream belonged to the now-unmounted instance → first message + its response are lost. Second attempt works because `activeConversationId` is already set, so no key change, no remount.

"Brand-new patient, type without clicking New" is the same path: the panel starts at `conversationId=null`, first send creates → remount → loss.

## Fix

Decouple the panel's React `key` (mount identity) from `activeConversationId`:
- Key the ChatPanel on `panelMountId` ONLY. It is already bumped by the user-driven `handleSelect` / `handleNew` — the only moments a true remount is desired.
- `onConversationCreated` should update sidebar highlight (`activeConversationId`) + `listVersion`, but NOT anything in the mount key.
- Guard the hydrate path too: the `conversationId` prop passed to ChatPanel must not flip undefined→id on the LIVE instance, or the `[initialConversationId]` effect (`ChatPanel.tsx:130-165`) re-fires and clobbers in-flight messages via the prop path instead of the key path. Cleanest: track a separate `mountedConversationId` (set only by select/new) for the hydrate prop + key, leaving `activeConversationId` purely for sidebar highlighting.

## Why CI never caught it

The chat E2E (pablo-saas THERAPY-hd4h) is API-only — it hits `/api/chat/*` directly with no browser, so a React remount race is invisible to it. THERAPY-z3a5 (the known flaky chat E2E) is a DIFFERENT race (empty assistant message on SSE timeout in save-as-note), not this.

## Acceptance

- [ ] First message in a new chat persists and streams a response — no "Loading conversation…" flash, no loss
- [ ] Same for "type on brand-new patient without clicking New"
- [ ] Switching to an existing conversation via the sidebar still remounts cleanly (no stale stream)
- [ ] Browser-level regression test added (see related E2E coverage note) — API-only won't catch this
close_reason: Decoupled ChatPanel mount key/hydrate prop from sidebar-highlight state (mountedConversationId vs activeConversationId). Added jsdom+RTL regression test (verified fail-on-bug). Closing with the PR.

title: Document download 401s — <a href> can't send bearer token
description: ## Symptom Clicking a document in the patient Documents list to download it returns **401 (not authenticated)**. No document can be downloaded. ## Root cause \`frontend/src/components/patients/PatientDocuments.tsx:250\` renders the download as a plain anchor: \`\`\`tsx Download \`\`\` which points at \`/api/documents/{id}/file\` (\`frontend/src/lib/api/patientDocuments.ts:107\`). That backend route (\`backend/app/routes/patient_documents.py:405\`, \`download_document_file\`) is gated by \`Depends(require_baa_acceptance)\` — it needs the Firebase **bearer token** in the \`Authorization\` header. A raw \`\` navigation only sends cookies, never custom headers, and Pablo auth is bearer-token (not cookie-session). So the request arrives unauthenticated and 401s before the route can mint the signed GCS URL and 302 to it. The signed-URL design implicitly assumed the browser would hit \`/file\` authenticated; with header-based auth, link navigation can't. ## Fix options 1. **Return the signed URL as JSON, open it client-side (recommended).** Add/adjust the route to return \`{ url: }\` with 200 (or keep the 302 and add a JSON sibling). Frontend calls it through the authenticated fetch client (bearer token attached), then \`window.open(url)\` / \`location.assign(url)\` to the GCS signed URL directly. The signed URL itself needs no auth header — GCS authorizes via the signature — so this cleanly separates app-auth from object-auth. Audit event still fires server-side when the URL is minted. 2. Fetch \`/file\` with \`redirect: \"manual\"\`, read the \`Location\` header, then navigate. Riskier: forwarding the Authorization header into a cross-origin GCS redirect can make GCS reject the request; manual redirect handling across origins is fiddly. 3. Cookie-session auth for this one endpoint — rejected, diverges from the app's bearer-token model. Recommend option 1. ## Relationship to patient-ux-refactor epic The planned \`DocumentViewerSheet\` (design/patient-ux-refactor.md, Phase 1) loads the same signed-URL path to render PDFs/images inline. It MUST use the authenticated-fetch-then-open pattern from option 1, not a raw URL. **This bead is effectively a prerequisite for the viewer bead** — fix the download contract first, then the viewer reuses it. ## Acceptance - [ ] Clicking Download on a document returns the file, not a 401 - [ ] Works for all three categories (chart, therapist_private, psychotherapy_notes) - [ ] The patient-document-access audit event still fires server-side - [ ] Frontend obtains the signed URL via the authenticated API client (bearer token), then navigates to GCS - [ ] No token ever placed in a URL/query string
notes: PR #281 (claude/47h-document-download-signed-url) — /file returns {url} JSON, frontend fetches via authenticated client then navigates to signed GCS URL. Close on merge.

title: Per-tenant alembic fan-out is not thread-safe — default to serial
description:
`backend/app/db/migrate_tenants.fan_out` parallelizes `command.upgrade` calls across N tenant schemas using a ThreadPoolExecutor (default 8 workers). Alembic's EnvironmentContext is a process-global singleton, so concurrent calls into `command.upgrade` race on it — the second thread to call `context.configure` corrupts the first's state.

Symptom: no-op fan-out runs (every tenant already at head) pass cleanly, hiding the bug indefinitely. The first multi-tenant DDL after the parallelism was enabled fails on every tenant at once — observed today against ~19 schemas during the patient_documents OCR column migration. Serializing with `PABLO_MIGRATE_MAX_WORKERS=1` makes it pass.

Compounding the diagnosis: alembic's env.py calls `fileConfig()` at import, which wipes the root logger's handlers each time it runs. The per-tenant `logger.info`/`logger.exception` output never made it to Cloud Logging — only stdout `print()` calls did. Whatever path eventually re-enables parallelism should also fix this so the next failure is diagnosable on first occurrence.

Default flipped to 1 in the meantime. To re-enable parallelism safely, options worth exploring:
- Subprocess-per-tenant (each child has its own EnvironmentContext)
- Run alembic offline (`--sql`) per tenant and apply DDL ourselves
- Replace alembic at the fan-out layer with a thinner runner that drives migration scripts directly without context globals

Acceptance: fan-out can run with > 1 worker against multiple tenants with real DDL without context corruption. Per-tenant tracebacks surface in Cloud Logging on failure.

title: Note-type registry: per-definition system prompt for generation
description:
## Problem

The note-generation pipeline is registry-driven: a NoteTypeDefinition can supply a custom user-prompt builder (`prompt_builder`), and every other type gets a prompt auto-synthesized from its fields' `ai_hint`s. But the SYSTEM prompt is fixed: `_DEFAULT_GENERATION_PROMPT_SYSTEM` (backend/app/services/note_generation_service.py:95) frames every transcript as a therapy session and instructs "clinically-appropriate language", with SOAP the only exception (SOAP_SYSTEM_PROMPT).

A registered note type whose format is not classic clinical narration (e.g. a supervision case review, a practice/admin format, or any downstream-registered format) can only fight the clinical system framing from inside the user prompt. That works but is fragile — the two prompts pull in different directions.

## Design

1. `NoteTypeDefinition` (backend/app/notes/registry.py) gains an optional `system_prompt: str | None = None` (a plain string, not a builder — system prompts are static per format; use `field(compare=False)` only if needed to keep dataclass equality semantics unchanged for existing tests).
2. `RegistryNoteGenerationService._generate_via_registry` (backend/app/services/note_generation_service.py:214-232) selects the system prompt in this order:
   - `definition.system_prompt` when set;
   - else `SOAP_SYSTEM_PROMPT` when `definition.key == SOAP_KEY` (unchanged);
   - else `_DEFAULT_GENERATION_PROMPT_SYSTEM` (unchanged).
   The selection must apply on BOTH branches (custom `prompt_builder` and auto-synthesized user prompt).
3. NOT exposed over the API: `NoteTypeSchema` in backend/app/routes/note_types.py must not serialize `system_prompt` (prompt text is server-side config, same as `prompt_builder` today).
4. No behavior change for any currently-registered type: `soap` and `narrative` definitions do not set the field.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `NoteTypeDefinition(system_prompt="...")` compiles and registers; default is None.
- [ ] Generation for a definition WITH `system_prompt` sends exactly that string as the system prompt (assert via the fake/mock LLM gateway capture in backend/tests/test_note_generation_service.py).
- [ ] Generation for `soap` still sends SOAP_SYSTEM_PROMPT; a hint-synthesized type without the field still sends the default (regression assertions).
- [ ] The custom-`prompt_builder` branch also honors `system_prompt` (test with a definition that sets both).
- [ ] `GET /api/note-types` response shape is unchanged (no `system_prompt` key) — assert in backend/tests/test_note_types_api.py.
- [ ] `make check` green (ruff + mypy + full pytest).

## Files

- backend/app/notes/registry.py (field)
- backend/app/services/note_generation_service.py (selection)
- backend/tests/test_notes_registry.py, backend/tests/test_note_generation_service.py, backend/tests/test_note_types_api.py

Small, self-contained, no DB/schema/API-surface change.

title: Dependabot auto-merge runs no post-merge workflows: merge with an App token
description:
'.github/workflows/dependabot-automerge.yml' merges with 'GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'. GitHub deliberately does not trigger push-based workflows for commits pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN, so nothing runs on the resulting merge commit: no CI, no Release, no Deploy.

Consequences on main:
  - No container image is published for those commits, so anything that pins a specific main SHA cannot resolve an image for it.
  - There is no post-merge verification at all on the default branch, so a merge that is green as a PR is never re-checked against main.
  - The gap is silent. Nothing reports failure; the workflows simply never start.

Observed on main 2026-07-25/26: commits from #613 and #617 have zero workflow runs (only CodeQL, which triggers on a different event). #619, merged by a person the same day, ran CI, Release and Deploy normally. That contrast is the whole bug.

Note this is unrelated to #612, which changed WHICH pull requests qualify for auto-merge (gating on pull_request.user.login rather than the spoofable github.actor). That fix is correct and still needed; it just does not affect which token performs the merge.

Fix: mint a short-lived GitHub App token (actions/create-github-app-token) and merge with that instead, so the merge is attributed to the App and downstream push workflows fire. Verify by confirming a Release run and a published image exist for the next auto-merged commit.
notes:
NOT SUITABLE FOR UNATTENDED AUTOMATION — needs a maintainer, assessed 2026-07-26.

Two reasons, both structural rather than a matter of difficulty:

1. Not self-contained. The fix is only partly a repo change. It also requires a GitHub App installed on this repository and its APP_ID / APP_PRIVATE_KEY provisioned as repo secrets — console and credential work that cannot be done from a checkout, and that no automated run should be doing.

2. No done-signal any pre-merge check can adjudicate. Correctness here means 'a later auto-merged dependency PR produces a Release run and a published image'. CI can validate workflow syntax; it cannot observe post-merge trigger behaviour. That is exactly why this went unnoticed across two merges on 2026-07-25/26.

It is also small: once the App and secrets exist, the workflow edit is a few lines, and the pattern is already written and commented in a sibling repository's base-bump workflow. Verification is observational — watch the next auto-merged dependency PR and confirm a Release run and image exist for its commit.

title: Pin fastapi <0.140: 0.140 retains dependency callables and leaks DB engines
description:
fastapi 0.140.0 adds three process-global caches in fastapi/dependencies/models.py:

  @lru_cache(maxsize=1024)
  def _is_gen_callable_cached(call_identity: _CallIdentity) -> bool

keyed by _CallIdentity, which holds a STRONG reference to the dependency callable (self.call is other.call). 0.139 has no such caches.

A session dependency is typically a closure capturing a SQLAlchemy Engine. Pinning the callable pins the closure, which pins the engine and its connection pool. SQLAlchemy releases pooled sockets on engine finalization, so a pinned engine never closes its connections. Any test suite that constructs many app instances therefore accumulates open connections until Postgres max_connections (default 100) is exhausted, failing with 'FATAL: sorry, too many clients already'.

Measured, holding every other dependency constant (sqlalchemy, psycopg2, testcontainers identical; only fastapi varied):
  - engines still reachable after gc.collect(): 50/50 under 0.140.0, 1/50 under 0.139.0
  - an integration suite that builds many apps: 93 failed / 219 passed under 0.140.0, clean under 0.139.0

Not a per-request regression: dependency cache sharing is unchanged (1 session opened and closed per request in both versions), so a single long-lived app process is not affected -- the engine there is already cached for the process lifetime.

Fix: constrain fastapi to >=0.139.0,<0.140 in pyproject.toml and relock. No security exposure in staying on 0.139.0 -- the only fastapi advisories are GHSA-8h2j-cgx8-6xv7 (< 0.65.2) and GHSA-qf9m-vfgh-m389 (<= 0.109.0).

Follow-up: report upstream (a global lru_cache strong-keyed on user callables retains everything those callables close over), then lift the pin once released.

title: Session validity: read-only session peek endpoint + server-driven idle controller
description: The client-side idle timer and the server idle clock (Redis) run independently, so a restored tab can render the app while the backend session is already expired, and the warning dialog can promise 'stay signed in' without extending the server session. Plan: (1) GET /api/auth/session — read-only peek returning {enforced, active, seconds_remaining} that does NOT refresh the activity TTL; (2) POST /api/auth/session/touch — explicit keep-alive; (3) rework IdleTimeout to validate the session on mount/pageshow/visibilitychange and poll, driving the countdown from the server clock, with the current local-clock behavior kept as fallback when enforcement is off (no Redis); (4) route SSE and blob-download 401s through the same forced-logout path as apiClient; (5) carry a reason param on the dashboard layout's dead-session redirect and let /login render for forced-logout arrivals instead of bouncing valid-cookie users back to /dashboard.

title: Terminal token-expiry 401 strands the user instead of redirecting to /login
description:
When a client-managed session terminally expires (the id token is expired AND the force-refresh retry cannot mint a valid token — e.g. the refresh token itself has expired after long inactivity, the account was disabled, or getIdToken returns null), an API call such as opening a patient comes back 401 and the user is NOT redirected to the login screen. They stay on a logged-in-looking page that renders a generic error.

Root cause: frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts only redirects to /login for the IDLE_TIMEOUT error code (handleIdleTimeoutLogout, ~line 239-245). The recoverable token path (TOKEN_EXPIRED/INVALID_TOKEN) force-refreshes and retries once (PR #300, ~line 189-194), but if that retry is STILL 401 it falls through to 'throw apiError' with no redirect. Next.js middleware doesn't catch it because the request is a client-side XHR, not a full navigation.

Fix: after the force-refresh retry, if a token-level 401 (TOKEN_EXPIRED/INVALID_TOKEN) persists — or the auth header could not be minted — treat it as terminal: signOut() + redirect to /login?reason=session_expired, mirroring handleIdleTimeoutLogout including its re-entry guard (a dashboard load fires several parallel requests, so a burst of 401s must produce ONE redirect, not many).

title: SOAP generation worker holds a DB connection across the model call
description:
generate_session_note (the async SOAP worker) loads the session, patient, and existing-note rows, which opens a read transaction and checks out a pooled connection. Nothing commits it before _generate_and_persist_note runs the multi-second model call, so the connection sits idle-in-transaction for the whole generation. On longer transcripts the server/proxy drops the idle connection; the note INSERT afterward then fails with OperationalError ('SSL connection has been closed unexpectedly') followed by PendingRollbackError, the note never persists, and the Cloud Tasks job retries the same session indefinitely (500 each time). The method's own comment already claims 'the LLM call runs with no open DB transaction' -- but no commit exists between the SELECTs and the model call.

Fix: commit the read transaction (release the pooled connection) immediately before generation, matching the either-side-of-the-LLM pattern upload_session already uses. expire_on_commit=False keeps the loaded session/patient usable, transcript is a JSONB column (no lazy reload), and the note INSERT autobegins a fresh pre-pinged connection that the checkout/after_begin listeners re-arm with search_path + RLS. Short transcripts hid the bug (generation finishes before the idle connection is dropped).

title: Stale Firebase session wedges the auth boot on sign-in
description:
useFirebaseAuthState awaited getIdToken() and the /api/login cookie sync before clearing its loading state, with no error handling. When a browser profile holds a restored Firebase session whose refresh token has expired, getIdToken() rejects, the onIdTokenChanged listener dies before setLoading(false), and the app is stuck on the loading splash (loading stays true, user stays null, so the redirect to /dashboard never fires). The existing stuck-state recovery only matches one specific SDK assertion, not a rejected refresh. Sign-in succeeds at the backend but the SPA never advances; a clean profile works because there is no stale token to refresh.

Fix (PR #502): wrap the listener in try/finally so loading always clears, bound the token refresh and cookie sync with a timeout, and on failure drop the stale session (signOut + wipe the persisted auth record + clear the cookie) so the next attempt starts clean. Cookie sync stays awaited on the success path because route middleware gates /dashboard on it. Adds client.test.ts.

title: Passkey-first onboarding leaves the new session without a second-factor claim (403 on PHI routes)
description:
Symptom: after completing onboarding with a passkey as the second factor, the user lands on the dashboard but every PHI route (e.g. GET /api/patients, GET /api/sessions) returns 403 MFA_REQUIRED. Confirmed in a live deployment; signing out and signing back in *with the passkey* clears it.

Root cause: require_mfa accepts a session only if the ID token carries firebase.sign_in_second_factor (Firebase TOTP/SMS) OR pablo_amr: ["webauthn"] (see backend/app/auth/providers.py:second_factor_satisfied). The pablo_amr claim is minted ONLY by POST /api/auth/passkey/authenticate/finish. Onboarding runs register/begin + register/finish (backend/app/routes/passkey.py): register/finish sets mfa_enrolled_at (which completes onboarding) and issues backup codes, but never mints a second-factor token. So the just-enrolled session holds a first-factor-only token and is blocked from all PHI until the user signs out and signs back in via the passkey (which runs the authenticate ceremony). Enrolling a passkey != the session has cleared MFA, and nothing in the onboarding flow does the step-up.

Impact: blocks 100% of passkey-first onboards from accessing any patient data on their first session. Launch-relevant.

Preferred fix: have POST /api/auth/passkey/register/finish mint and return a pablo_amr custom token on a successful attestation. A verified attestation proves possession of the authenticator at that moment, just like an assertion, so it is legitimate to treat the freshly-enrolled session as second-factor-satisfied. The client then signs in with the returned custom token and force-refreshes the Firebase ID token before redirecting to the dashboard — no second WebAuthn ceremony, no sign-out/in. One ceremony total.

Rejected alternative: client runs the authenticate ceremony immediately after register/finish. Makes the user effectively perform the WebAuthn ceremony twice.

Acceptance:
- A brand-new passkey-first onboard can load patient data immediately after finishing onboarding, with no sign-out/in.
- register/finish returns a token (or signal) the client uses to obtain an ID token whose claims satisfy second_factor_satisfied.
- Regression test: a session established directly from register/finish (first enrollment) passes require_mfa. Keep the existing authenticate/finish -> pablo_amr path working.
- Note for the second-passkey-from-settings case: that session is already MFA-satisfied, so minting is redundant but harmless; ensure it does not regress.
notes: PR pablo#494 (backend mint + OSS api type). Paired SaaS overlay consumer: pablo-saas#707 / THERAPY-rokd (RED until base-bump).

title: Clinician must author/review bundled MDD/GAD criterion wording before any clinical use
description:
GATE before the diagnostic engine's bundled content is exposed in any real/clinical deployment.

The MDD/GAD criterion + gate wording in backend/app/diagnostics/baseline.py (BASELINE_DEFINITIONS) is original DRAFT content, almost certainly AI-drafted (PR #378), committed without AI attribution and NOT authored or reviewed by a clinician. The structure tracks DSM-5 closely (5-of-9 + 2 cardinals + exclusion gates; GAD worry + 3-of-6 + 6mo).

Two risks:
1. Clinical accuracy — an LLM paraphrase can be subtly wrong in a tool that SUGGESTS a diagnosis (patient-safety surface). Determination is clinician-confirmed, but the criterion text is presented as authoritative.
2. Copyright — a paraphrase of DSM-5 criteria can still be a derivative of APA-copyrighted text even with no verbatim copying. 'We paraphrased it' is not automatically a clean-room defense.

Done so far: record dialog now shows a 'Draft criteria — for clinical review before clinical use; not a substitute for clinical judgment' notice (PABLO-6xj.2, PR #381, commit 4c4f33b). Draft doc for review: docs/architecture/diagnostic-content-mdd.draft.md (uncommitted).

Required: (a) the clinical lead authors or rewrites _MDD/_GAD wording and signs off; (b) explicit decision on the DSM-5 derivative/copyright question (legal sanity check); (c) only then remove/relax the draft marker. Until both, treat bundled content as draft-only.
notes: Author MDD/GAD as clinician-authored CHECKLISTS (clinician marks which symptoms apply; no X-of-Y threshold, no auto 'meets criteria') sourced solely from PHQ-9/GAD-7 (Pfizer free-use grant) + peer-reviewed open literature; ICD-11 cite-only. Sourcing analysis (AI-drafted, pending human clinical + legal review): pablo-saas docs/compliance/diagnostic-symptom-sourcing-research.md. Gates before bundling any content / relaxing the in-product draft marker: (1) clinical-lead authorship + sign-off; (2) legal sign-off on the PHQ-9/GAD-7 grant + non-DSM provenance. Engine + public-domain ICD-10-CM catalog already in place; no definitions bundled by default.

title: enable_rls_on_schema leaves three tenant tables deny-all (FORCE RLS, no policy)
description:
enable_rls_on_schema (backend/app/db/__init__.py) selects every tenant table that has a user_id, patient_id, or id column, then ENABLE+FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY at the top of the loop *before* deciding a policy. It then creates a policy only for known shapes (patient_documents, patient_clinicians, patients, any-user_id, any-patient_id, chat_messages). A table that has only an 'id' column and matches no shape ends up force-RLS'd with NO policy = deny-all: under a NOBYPASSRLS role every read returns 0 rows and every write affects 0 rows, silently.

Audit of the current tenant template finds THREE such tables:
  - compliance_documents — owns rows via uploaded_by_user_id (NOT NULL); the code only checks the literal column name user_id, so it misses this owner column. LIVE feature (compliance_document repo get/list/query).
  - ehr_routes — no ownership column at all (ehr_system/route_name/steps); tenant-level config like ehr_prompts, which is correctly skipped only because it lacks an id column. LIVE feature (ehr_route repo).
  - users — vestigial per-tenant table, unused at runtime (identity lives in the platform schema); a Firestore-migration relic, frozen at an older column shape.

Only invisible until the role lost BYPASSRLS — BYPASSRLS ignores RLS entirely, so deny-all read fine. Existing tenants were not backfilled, so the blast radius is tenants provisioned after the role flip: their compliance-document and EHR-route features silently return nothing.

The chat_messages branch already documents this exact trap ('the loop ENABLE+FORCEs RLS but leaves no policy, which is a deny-all configuration that only the BYPASSRLS-on-role posture mistakenly hides in production') — these three tables are the siblings nobody added branches for.

FIX:
  1. compliance_documents — add a policy keyed on uploaded_by_user_id (USING + WITH CHECK). uploaded_by_user_id is NOT NULL; prefer it over the nullable compliance_item_id parent so orphan documents are not hidden.
  2. ehr_routes + users — treat as not-row-scoped (search_path is their boundary): do NOT force RLS on them (idempotently DISABLE to heal any tenant already provisioned wrong). users is also slated for removal (see cleanup below).
  3. Fail-loud guard: restructure so RLS is only forced when a policy is attached (or the table is on an explicit not-row-scoped list); raise on any id/user_id/patient_id table that matches neither, so a future table cannot silently become deny-all.

title: Audit writes: enforce tenant scope + surface failures via a pluggable notifier
description: Audit entries are written to tenant-scoped tables (audit_logs) resolved by the connection search_path. Two integrity gaps: (1) the write relies on AMBIENT search_path — a write on a connection without an established tenant context can resolve against the wrong/no schema, yielding an inaccurate or cross-contaminated audit trail (an authoritative record that under-reports for one tenant and is polluted for another); (2) the audit service currently SWALLOWS write failures (best-effort log), so a dropped entry is silent — undetectable incompleteness. Harden: (a) assert an established tenant context before an audit write (fail loudly if absent) instead of relying on ambient state; (b) replace the silent swallow with a structured, high-severity 'audit integrity' event emitted through a PLUGGABLE AuditFailureNotifier interface (default impl: structured CRITICAL log line with a stable, machine-consumable marker). title: Pentest severity rollup uses substring match on report prose — every run trips HIGH/CRITICAL alert
description:
Background
==========

`pentest_runner._highest_severity()` returns "CRITICAL" if the literal
string "CRITICAL" appears anywhere in the assembled report markdown:

    def _highest_severity(report: str) -> str:
        for token in ("CRITICAL", "HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW"):
            if token in report:
                return token
        return "NONE"

Every report inevitably contains the word "CRITICAL" — in the
executive summary ("**CRITICAL:** 0 findings"), in the methodology
prose, and most damningly in **Appendix C: Severity Rubric** which
defines what CRITICAL means. So every run logs `severity=CRITICAL`
regardless of the actual finding set.

This was masked for weeks because `_notify_high_finding` was emitting
via the default Python logger (which doesn't end up in
`jsonPayload.severity`), so the Cloud Logging alert policy silently
missed every prior run. Once `_notify_high_finding` was fixed to emit
structured JSON the policy filters on, the underlying false-positive
in `_highest_severity` started paging on every run.

Confirmed across runs 2026-05-18, 2026-05-24, and 2026-05-25 — all
three logged `severity=CRITICAL` despite having zero findings in the
narrative.

Connected bug
=============

`_count_findings_by_severity` is the sibling function the author
clearly intended to be the right pattern (comment: "avoids re-parsing
the LLM narrative for severity counts"). But it counts rows by
matching `| CRITICAL |` against the report — i.e. it expects the LLM
to render findings in a `| Severity | Title | Location | ... |`
table. The current narrative renders findings as bullet prose
("**MEDIUM:** 1 finding") instead, so this function has been
returning `{CRITICAL: 0, HIGH: 0, MEDIUM: 0, LOW: 0}` for every run,
including ones with real medium findings.

Both bugs share a root cause: alerting is computed from the LLM-
generated markdown rather than from the structured scanner outputs
the runner already has in hand.

Fix
===

The collectors already produce structured `by_severity` dicts as part
of each artifact's summary (`run_trivy_image`, `run_pip_audit`, etc.).
Roll severity up deterministically from those, not from the report
prose. Keep the LLM in the narrative role only — it makes the report
readable, but it does not have the pager.

Concretely:

1. Compute `finding_counts` and `highest_severity` from
   `artifact.summary["by_severity"]` aggregated across collectors,
   before the LLM call.
2. Pass those values into the prompt so the narrative is constrained
   to match (LLM cannot drift the severity).
3. Replace both `_highest_severity` and `_count_findings_by_severity`
   to read from the pre-computed counts, not the assembled report.
4. Add a `pentest/suppressions.yaml` for tracked false-positives and
   context-aware downgrades (e.g. semgrep `sqlalchemy.text` flags
   with bound params; `urllib` usage in `pentest_identity.py`).
   Schema: `{tool, finding_id, downgrade_to, reason, expires_on,
   approved_by}`. Apply suppressions during the deterministic rollup,
   not in prose.

Why this matters
================

This is a HIPAA-relevant alert path. The automated pentest mechanism
contributes to §164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A) (continuous risk analysis) and
to the §164.314(a) written-verification trail. An alert that fires on
every run trains the operator to ignore it — alert fatigue is the
failure mode that masks the next real finding. The substring bug
makes the alert literally untrustable.

Concrete evidence
=================

- Latest run report (compliance bucket): pentest/2026-05-25T20-41-02Z-
  a41fa42f.md, narrative summary 0 critical, 0 high, 1 medium, 3 low
- Log line: `Pentest report=... severity=CRITICAL`
- Same log line for runs 2026-05-18, 2026-05-24, 2026-05-25
- Cloud Logging alert policy filters on `jsonPayload.alert_type=
  "pentest_high"` emitted by `_notify_high_finding`

Out of scope
============

- Adding a UI for managing suppressions. `pentest/suppressions.yaml`
  + git review is sufficient.
- Migrating away from the LLM narrative. The judgment value is real;
  it just shouldn't drive alerting.
- Backfilling severity for prior runs in the audit log.

title: Patient list has no pagination — UI caps at 20 rows
description:
## Problem

\`PatientTable.tsx\` calls \`usePatientList({ search })\` with no \`page_size\` and no \`page\` controls. The backend default is \`page_size=20\` (\`backend/app/routes/patients.py:163\`), so the UI silently truncates to the first 20 patients sorted by last_name, first_name. There is no Next/Prev, no \"showing N of M\", and no way for a clinician with 21+ patients to reach the rest of their roster except by typing into the search box.

The backend response already returns \`total\` alongside \`data\` (\`PatientListResponse\`), so the data is there — the UI just discards it.

## Why it matters

For solo therapists this caps usable size at 20 active clients. As soon as one provider has more — totally normal for an established practice — they cannot see their full list without searching by name (which has its own UX issues, see [[patient-search-needs-improvement]]).

## Options

1. **Add pagination controls.** Standard Prev/Next + page indicator. Honest \"showing 1-20 of N\" framing. Minimal change.
2. **Increase the default page_size + infinite scroll.** Friendlier on small lists. More work, but matches how the table feels for someone with 35 patients.
3. **Increase the default page_size to 100 and call it a day.** API max is already 100; cheapest fix. Caps later instead of at 20.

Recommendation: option 3 short-term (one-line fix: \`usePatientList({ search, page_size: 100 })\`), then revisit pagination/infinite-scroll if any practice grows past 100.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A user with >20 patients can see them all in the UI
- [ ] Page shows the actual \`total\` somewhere so users know what they're looking at
- [ ] Tests cover the chosen page_size
close_reason: Patient list: page_size=100 + 'Showing N of M' total (y93); substring search across both names, search_by toggle dropped, generic placeholder (bgr). Closing with the PR.

title: Grant documentai.apiUser to prod backend SA
description:
## Problem

On 2026-05-24 we wired the Document AI OCR processor into Cloud Run for both pablohealth-dev and pablohealth-prod. Dev is fully functional. **Prod backend SA does not have \`roles/documentai.apiUser\`**, so when the OCR fallback fires it will get an auth-denied error from the Document AI API instead of successfully OCR'ing.

The Cloud Run env vars are already set on prod (revision pablo-backend-00249-qcp) — only the IAM grant is missing. Dev's backend SA already has this role, which is why dev works.

## Why this wasn't done automatically

Cross-environment IAM-modifying gcloud commands are blocked in the Claude Code harness on prod targets. The dev grant was done manually before the deploy; prod's was missed.

## The one-liner

\`\`\`bash
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding pablohealth-prod \\
  --member=serviceAccount:pablo-backend@pablohealth-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \\
  --role=roles/documentai.apiUser \\
  --condition=None
\`\`\`

## Verify

After granting, upload a scanned PDF in prod and confirm the \"OCR not yet supported\" badge doesn't appear on the document row.

## Acceptance

- [ ] \`gcloud projects get-iam-policy pablohealth-prod\` shows pablo-backend SA with documentai.apiUser
- [ ] Scanned PDF upload in prod produces extracted_text (visible via patient document detail endpoint or chat citation manifest)

title: Coalesce read-access audit writes within an active-record window
description:
A clinician working in one chart generates many reads -- opening a session, the frontend refetching on focus/navigation, etc. -- and each currently writes a separate *_viewed audit row + Cloud Logging mirror. Over a week of light single-user testing we already saw hundreds of patient_viewed/session_listed rows; this scales per active clinician and every row lands in the 6-year retention-locked sink. The signal we actually want is 'clinician accessed patient X during a work window,' not one row per HTTP GET.

Add a coalescing gate in AuditService for the read actions (patient_viewed, session_viewed, chat_conversation_viewed, patient_document_viewed). Use Redis (the same instance backing rate-limit/idle-session) as a dedup gate: key on (user_id, action, target_id) with a configurable TTL window (~10-15 min). On a cache miss, write the audit row as today and set the key; on a hit, skip the dual-write. Postgres stays the synchronous system-of-record -- Redis is ONLY a 'have we already recorded this access recently?' gate, never a buffer or store for the events themselves.

Critical: fail OPEN. If Redis is unavailable or errors, fall through and write the audit row. For audit the safe failure is an extra duplicate row, never a dropped access -- the opposite of idle_session's fail-closed posture. Make the window TTL a setting (default off / 0 = no coalescing, so self-hosters without Redis keep today's behavior unchanged). Consider NOT coalescing the restricted-category document views (psychotherapy_notes) so those keep full fidelity.
design:
## Implementation design — read-access audit coalescing

### Where it goes
All read audits funnel through `AuditService.log(...)` → `AuditService._persist(entry)`
in `backend/app/services/audit_service.py`. Add the gate as an early return at
the top of `_persist`. Reuse the existing Redis access pattern
(`from ..redis_client import get_redis_client`, gated by `settings.use_redis`),
same as `rate_limit.py` / `auth/idle_session.py`.

### Setting (settings.py)
    audit_read_coalesce_seconds: int = Field(
        default=0,  # 0 = off; self-hosters without Redis keep today's behavior
        description="Coalesce duplicate read-access audit events per (user, record) within this window.",
    )

### Code (audit_service.py)
    _COALESCED_READ_ACTIONS = frozenset({
        AuditAction.PATIENT_VIEWED,
        AuditAction.SESSION_VIEWED,
        AuditAction.CHAT_CONVERSATION_VIEWED,   # added in PABLO-m1y
        AuditAction.PATIENT_DOCUMENT_VIEWED,
        # NOT *_VIEWED_RESTRICTED — psychotherapy notes keep full fidelity
    })

    def _should_skip_duplicate(self, entry: AuditLogEntry) -> bool:
        """True if an identical read by this user was already recorded in the window.

        Fails OPEN: any Redis problem -> write the row. For audit the safe
        failure is a duplicate, never a dropped access (inverse of idle_session,
        which fails closed for security).
        """
        ttl = get_settings().audit_read_coalesce_seconds
        if ttl <= 0 or entry.action not in {a.value for a in _COALESCED_READ_ACTIONS}:
            return False
        try:
            redis = get_redis_client()
            if redis is None:
                return False
            key = f"audit:seen:{entry.user_id}:{entry.action}:{entry.resource_id}"
            first_time = redis.set(key, "1", nx=True, ex=ttl)  # True if set, None if key exists
            return first_time is None
        except Exception:
            logger.warning("Audit coalesce check failed; writing row (fail-open)", exc_info=True)
            return False

    def _persist(self, entry: AuditLogEntry) -> None:
        if self._should_skip_duplicate(entry):
            return
        # ... existing PHI-free assert + repo.append + Cloud Logging dual-write unchanged ...

### Why this shape
- `SET key 1 NX EX ttl` is atomic (no GET-then-SET race), cross-instance, TTL built in.
- FIXED window (key expires ttl after FIRST access, not extended on hits) -> records
  "accessed patient X" ~once per ttl of continuous work. Guarantees at least one durable
  access record per work window. Do NOT make it sliding (could suppress for hours).
- Per-(user, action, resource_id) key -> two different patients still log two rows; only
  repeats of the SAME record collapse.
- Postgres stays the synchronous system-of-record. Redis only decides WHETHER to write,
  never holds the event. (Redis-as-store would be a HIPAA durability gap — explicitly out.)
- Off by default; flip on via deploy env (audit_read_coalesce_seconds=900 ~ 15 min).

### Tests
1. Two patient_viewed for same (user, patient) within window -> 1 row; different patients -> 2 rows.
2. Redis raising -> every row still written (fail-open). Use a fake redis whose .set raises.
3. Restricted document view (PATIENT_DOCUMENT_VIEWED_RESTRICTED) -> never coalesced.
4. audit_read_coalesce_seconds=0 -> behaves exactly as today (no Redis calls).

### Sequencing
Best landed together with PABLO-m1y (which adds the CHAT_CONVERSATION_VIEWED action this set
references, and removes the noisy *_listed events). If fj1 ships first, drop
CHAT_CONVERSATION_VIEWED from the set until m1y lands.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated reads of the same record by the same user within the window produce one audit row; Redis outage falls back to writing every row (verified by test); restricted document views optionally exempt; coalescing is config-gated and off by default; per-record first-access still always recorded.

title: Refactor auth token verification to Chain of Responsibility — eliminate unverified JWT peek
description:
## Why this issue exists

The current multi-issuer JWT verification flow has a structural flaw: it peeks at the token's `iss` claim *without* verifying the signature (`jwt.decode(token, options={"verify_signature": False})`) to route to the right verifier, then the selected verifier re-checks the signature downstream. This is safe (the second verify is the real one), but it is architecturally wrong — a nosemgrep annotation suppresses the Semgrep rule that correctly flags it, and future devs have to understand a two-step trust model that shouldn't exist. Raised as PABLO-001 in the 2026-05-31 pentest report.

## Current code structure

File: `backend/app/auth/service.py`

```
_unverified_issuer(token) -> str | None
    jwt.decode(token, verify_signature=False)  # ← the problem
    returns iss claim for routing only

_get_verifier_registry() -> VerifierRegistry   # lru_cached
    builds from settings:
      VerifierRegistry(firebase=FirebaseVerifier(), oidc=OidcVerifier(...) if oidc_issuer else None)

verify_token(token) -> VerifiedIdentity
    issuer = _unverified_issuer(token)
    verifier = _get_verifier_registry().get_verifier(issuer)
    return verifier.verify(token)
```

File: `backend/app/auth/providers.py` — `VerifierRegistry` class

```python
class VerifierRegistry:
    def __init__(self, firebase: FirebaseVerifier, oidc: OidcVerifier | None) -> None:
        self._firebase = firebase
        self._by_issuer: dict[str, TokenVerifier] = {}
        if oidc is not None:
            self._by_issuer[oidc.issuer] = oidc

    def get_verifier(self, issuer: str | None) -> TokenVerifier:
        # OIDC if issuer matches, else Firebase catch-all
        if issuer is not None and issuer in self._by_issuer:
            return self._by_issuer[issuer]
        return self._firebase
```

`FirebaseVerifier` and `OidcVerifier` both implement `TokenVerifier` protocol: `verify(token: str) -> VerifiedIdentity`. They raise `HTTPException(401, ...)` on failure with specific error codes: `TOKEN_EXPIRED`, `TOKEN_REVOKED`, `USER_DISABLED`, `INVALID_TOKEN`.

## What to build — Chain of Responsibility

The registry's `verify()` method should try each verifier in order and return on first success. No pre-peek. No routing step outside the registry.

```python
# On VerifierRegistry:
def verify(self, token: str) -> VerifiedIdentity:
    first_exc: HTTPException | None = None
    for verifier in self._verifiers:  # ordered list: [firebase, oidc] if oidc configured
        try:
            return verifier.verify(token)
        except HTTPException as e:
            if e.status_code != 401:
                raise  # unexpected — propagate immediately
            if first_exc is None:
                first_exc = e  # preserve the first (most specific) error
    raise first_exc or HTTPException(status_code=401)
```

**Why first error, not last:** Firebase is first and handles >99% of tokens. Its error codes (TOKEN_EXPIRED, TOKEN_REVOKED) are what clients act on for re-auth logic. If we returned the last error, an expired Firebase token would fall through to OIDC (which rejects it as INVALID_TOKEN) and the client would get the wrong signal. OIDC in this system is only the pentest runner — its error quality does not matter.

**Performance:** Firebase fails fast on non-Firebase tokens at the `kid` lookup in its cached JWKS — no RSA operation occurs. The overhead for the OIDC path (Firebase fast-fail + OIDC verify) is a dict lookup, not a network call.

## What to delete / change

1. **Delete** `_unverified_issuer()` from `service.py` entirely — no longer needed.
2. **Delete** `get_verifier()` from `VerifierRegistry` — replaced by `verify()`.
3. **Add** `verify()` method to `VerifierRegistry` (see above).
4. **Change** `VerifierRegistry.__init__` to store `self._verifiers: list[TokenVerifier]` (ordered: firebase first, oidc appended if configured) instead of the `_by_issuer` dict + `_firebase` catch-all.
5. **Simplify** `verify_token()` in `service.py` to: `return _get_verifier_registry().verify(token)`
6. **Remove** the `# nosemgrep: python.jwt.security.unverified-jwt-decode` annotation from `service.py:236` — the offending line is gone.

## Acceptance criteria

- `verify_token()` in `service.py` has no `jwt.decode` call with `verify_signature=False`
- `_unverified_issuer()` is deleted
- `# nosemgrep` annotation on the old line is gone
- `VerifierRegistry.verify()` exists; `get_verifier()` is removed
- Expired/revoked Firebase token still returns `TOKEN_EXPIRED` / `TOKEN_REVOKED` (not OIDC's generic error)
- `make check` passes (ruff + mypy + pytest)
- Running semgrep locally produces 0 hits on `python.jwt.security.unverified-jwt-decode`

title: frontend(auth): wait for authStateReady before reading currentUser in apiClient
description:
Some authenticated requests go out with no Authorization header right after a sign-in transition (notably multiFactor.enroll() during the onboarding MFA step), because getAuthHeader reads getFirebaseAuth().currentUser synchronously while the SDK is briefly between users.

Decoding Playwright traces of a fresh-user onboarding run shows the post-MFA token re-issue lands correctly (next request has firebase.sign_in_second_factor='totp'), but the request that fires in the next tick after the enrollment frame closes — recordCompanionAction's POST /api/saas/users/me/companion, or the frontend's fe-error reporter — goes out with no Authorization header at all. Backend correctly 401s and the user sees a 'Couldn't save that' toast with no clear remediation.

#300's TOKEN_REFRESH_RETRY_CODES retry doesn't recover this case: there's no token to refresh, the if (currentUser) branch in getAuthHeader is simply skipped, and the retry hits the same null window.

Fix: in getAuthHeader, await getFirebaseAuth().authStateReady() before reading currentUser. authStateReady resolves the first time Firebase's auth state listener fires and is a no-op thereafter, so the cost is one microtask in steady state and the right amount of wait during the post-enrollment transition. Same edit applies to the SSE consumer that shares the helper.

Surfaced by chart-render-smoke.spec.ts via the onboardedUser fixture (browser.newContext() exposes the race more reliably than the test's default context). Repros consistently across two full dev e2e runs.
notes: PR #307 (https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/pull/307). One-helper change in frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts: await getFirebaseAuth().authStateReady() before reading currentUser, so requests fired during the multiFactor.enroll() transition wait for the new currentUser to install instead of going out with no Authorization header. SSE consumer (lib/chat/sse.ts) inherits the fix via shared getAuthHeader. eslint + tsc clean locally. Keep open until merged + bumped into pablo-saas via BASE_IMAGE.txt.

title: Validate audio magic bytes at /upload-audio boundary (reject non-audio synchronously)
description:
POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/upload-audio gates uploads on the client-declared Content-Type only (_ALLOWED_AUDIO_TYPES in app/routes/sessions.py). It never inspects the bytes, so a client can send arbitrary content labeled 'audio/wav' and pass the gate. The malformed payload then fails downstream in the async transcription worker (the RIFF sniff + wave.open in app/services/assemblyai_transcription_service.py), surfacing as a FAILED session via the polling task rather than a synchronous 4xx — an orphaned session the user only sees minutes later.

Add a lightweight magic-byte/header sniff at the upload boundary so non-audio is rejected synchronously:
  - WAV: 'RIFF'....'WAVE'
  - MP3: ID3 tag or 0xFFE* MPEG frame sync
  - OGG: 'OggS'
  - FLAC: 'fLaC'
  - MP4/M4A: 'ftyp' box at offset 4
  - WebM: EBML header 0x1A45DFA3

Keep the Content-Type allowlist as a cheap first pass; make the byte sniff the authoritative check. Reject mismatches with 415 (or 422). Apply to both audio parts. Add a unit test that a non-audio payload mislabeled as audio/* is rejected at the boundary, not enqueued.

title: Simplify chat source selection — drop unavailable sources, fix 'Selected sessions', add document picker
description:
## Problem

The chat source-chip rail (frontend/src/components/chat/SourceChipRail.tsx + sourceMeta.ts) exposes 10 sources, but most aren't usable today, so the UI reads as complex while doing little:

- **'Selected sessions' (progress_notes_explicit) is broken.** Toggling the chip sets the key to boolean `true` (ChatPanel.handleAddSource/handleToggleSource), but the backend loader requires `{note_ids:[...]}` (backend/app/services/chat_context_bundler.py:441) and raises InvalidSelectionError otherwise. There is no session-picker UI to supply note_ids. Net: selecting it does nothing useful or errors the turn. This is the user-reported "doesn't appear to do anything."
- **'Uploaded documents' (patient_documents) is all-or-nothing.** Toggling includes EVERY uploaded document. The backend already supports an explicit `ids` list (_load_patient_documents falls back to all-for-patient only when no ids given, chat_context_bundler.py:~569), but there's no UI to pick which documents.
- **Always-empty sources clutter the rail.** most_recent_intake, treatment_plan_active, safety_plan_active, current_medications reference note types (intake/treatment_plan/safety_plan/medications) not registered in the OSS note-type registry — only soap + narrative ship today (see comment chat_context_bundler.py:25-31). They always return row_count=0 / reason=no_data. lab_values_recent + vitals_recent have no data path in a therapy product.
- The "+ Add source" menu only hides sources flagged `module_not_available` in the latest manifest, and only AFTER the first turn — so on a fresh chat all 10 show.

## Asks

1. **Surface only sources with a working data path** in the chip rail + add-source menu: progress_notes_recent, patient_documents, pasted_text. Keep the backend loaders for the not-yet-registered note types (they're forward-compatible) but don't show chips for them until their note types actually ship.
2. **Remove the 'Selected sessions' chip** (progress_notes_explicit) for now — it's broken without a picker. If per-session selection is wanted later, file a follow-up to build a note-multiselect that supplies `note_ids` in the correct shape.
3. **Add a per-document picker** for patient_documents so the clinician can choose which uploaded documents to include (backend already supports the `ids` shape). Ties into the patient-documents UI work in this epic (PABLO-6x5.5).
4. Result: a short, honest source rail where every visible source works.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Source rail + add menu show only sources with a real data path (no always-empty chips on a fresh chat)
- [ ] No visible source can produce an InvalidSelectionError from a boolean-vs-shape mismatch
- [ ] 'Selected sessions' removed (or a working picker added)
- [ ] Uploaded documents can be included selectively, not only all-or-nothing
close_reason: Chat source rail gated to live-data sources (SUPPORTED_SOURCE_KEYS); Selected-sessions removed; pasted_text seeds {content} editor; patient_documents gets all-or-pick document picker; OSS default trimmed. Closing with the PR.

title: Patient search: clarify field + add substring match + expose first-name search
description:
## Problem

Three related UX gaps in the patient list search input (\`PatientTable.tsx:139\`):

1. **No indication search is last-name**. Placeholder says \"Search patients by name...\". The backend defaults \`search_by=last_name\` (\`backend/app/routes/patients.py:160\`), so typing a first name returns nothing — silently. Users assume their patient was deleted or the list is broken.

2. **Prefix-only matching**. The repo uses \`first_name_lower.startswith(search_lower)\` / \`last_name_lower.startswith(search_lower)\` (\`backend/app/repositories/patient.py:206-208\`). \"smith\" matches Smith; \"mith\" does not. Most users expect substring search (\"contains\"), especially when they remember the middle of a hyphenated last name or only a fragment.

3. **\`search_by\` query param is exposed in the API but never in the UI**. The route accepts \`search_by=first_name|last_name\` but \`usePatientList\` callers never pass it. There's no toggle, no dropdown, no smart heuristic (\"if input has a comma, split into last, first\").

## Options

**Minimum viable improvement:**
- Update placeholder to \`\"Search by last name...\"\` so the contract is honest
- Add a small \"First name\" toggle next to the search input

**Better:**
- Change \`startswith\` to \`contains\` (i.e., \`%search%\`) — substring match in both fields by default, no toggle needed. Repo + tests change in one place. Trade-off: substring on a large patient list is slower than prefix, but with the ILIKE pattern and lower-cased indexed columns it's fine through low-thousands rows.
- Drop the \`search_by\` param entirely; always search both fields.

**Best:**
- Substring search across \`first_name || ' ' || last_name\` so \"john smi\" works
- Optional: weight last-name matches higher in ranking
- Keep input copy as \"Search patients...\"

## Recommendation

Go directly to \"Better\" — substring search both fields, drop \`search_by\` toggle. It's the smallest change that produces the least surprising behavior. \"Best\" can follow if users still complain about full-name search.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Typing a middle fragment of a last name finds the patient (substring match)
- [ ] Typing a first name finds the patient (without any toggle)
- [ ] Placeholder text either matches actual behavior or behavior is broadened to match the generic placeholder
- [ ] Repo + route tests updated
close_reason: Patient list: page_size=100 + 'Showing N of M' total (y93); substring search across both names, search_by toggle dropped, generic placeholder (bgr). Closing with the PR.

title: Auto-derive Document AI project + processor at startup
description:
## Problem

The Document AI OCR client (\`backend/app/services/document_ai_ocr.py\`) gates on three env vars: \`DOCUMENT_AI_PROJECT_ID\`, \`DOCUMENT_AI_PROCESSOR_ID\`, \`DOCUMENT_AI_LOCATION\`. If any are unset, \`is_configured\` returns False, OCR silently falls back to \"unavailable\", and finalized scanned PDFs show \"OCR not yet supported — text extraction failed\" in the UI.

This is exactly how the feature broke when the OCR processors were provisioned in pablohealth-dev and pablohealth-prod on 2026-05-24 — the processors exist, the IAM role is granted (in dev), but no one wired the env vars into Cloud Run. The deploy isn't atomic, so we shipped a half-configured feature.

## Why most of this is redundant

1. **\`DOCUMENT_AI_PROJECT_ID\`** is always the same as the running GCP project. Cloud Run already injects \`GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT\` automatically (also \`GCP_PROJECT_ID\` in our config). \`google.auth.default()\` returns the project too. Asking operators to set this third copy is pure ceremony.

2. **\`DOCUMENT_AI_PROCESSOR_ID\`** is less trivially redundant — a project can hold many processors (OCR, Form Parser, Handwriting, etc.) — but in practice we always want \"the processor whose displayName is \`pablo-patient-doc-ocr\`\". That's discoverable at startup via \`processors.list\` with a name filter, cached for the lifetime of the process.

3. **\`DOCUMENT_AI_LOCATION\`** can default to \"us\" (where our processors live) and only be overridden if we ever need EU.

## Proposed change

In \`DocumentAiOcrClient\`:
- If \`document_ai_project_id\` is None, fall back to \`os.environ.get(\"GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT\")\` then \`google.auth.default()[1]\`.
- If \`document_ai_processor_id\` is None, on first call run \`processors.list(parent=...)\` filtered by displayName (constant \`PABLO_OCR_PROCESSOR_NAME = \"pablo-patient-doc-ocr\"\`); cache the resolved id on the instance.
- Log once at startup with the resolved values so it's obvious in logs which processor is being used.
- Keep the env vars as escape hatches for tests and local overrides.

Outcome: zero-config OCR in any environment where a processor exists with the canonical name. Provisioning becomes \"create the processor + grant the IAM role\" — no Cloud Run env-var update step.

## Acceptance

- [ ] OCR works in pablohealth-dev with no DOCUMENT_AI_* env vars set
- [ ] Tests still pass with explicit env vars (escape hatch preserved)
- [ ] Startup log shows the resolved project + processor id once
- [ ] Doc string on \`DocumentAiOcrClient\` updated to describe the resolution order

title: Absolute audit-log immutability via DB role separation (pablo_app runtime role)
description:
Follow-up to PABLO-5zy. The append-only trigger shipped in PR #432 is defense-in-depth, not absolute: the app shares the table-owner DB role (pablo) with the retention cron, so a fully-compromised app process could SET LOCAL app.allow_audit_purge='on' itself or ALTER TABLE audit_logs DISABLE TRIGGER. Absolute §164.312(c)(1) immutability requires DB role separation.

Verified design (2026-06-07): single Cloud SQL user 'pablo' owns all tenant tables; app + all Cloud Run jobs share one pablo-database-url secret; the app process itself does DDL (create_practice_schema at boot via ensure_schemas, and the pentest admin route), so it cannot be a pure low-priv role without a dual-engine split.

Plan:
- New cluster-level role 'pablo_app' (runtime, least-privilege). Created ONCE as a bootstrap step (gcloud sql users create + password in Secret Manager + new pablo-app-database-url secret) wired into setup-solo.sh; run manually against existing oss/dev/prod. NOT a per-tenant alembic migration (CREATE ROLE is cluster-level).
- Keep 'pablo' as the owner/DDL role used by provisioning, alembic, and the retention purge.
- Dual-engine: a privileged engine (pablo) for create_practice_schema + audit_retention purge; the low-priv engine (pablo_app) for normal request traffic. create_practice_schema already takes an engine arg, so the injection point is contained.
- Per-schema grants to pablo_app (full DML on most tables; SELECT,INSERT only on audit_logs) plus ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for future tables. Lives in tenant_template.sql + a backfill migration (same touch-points as the trigger).
- App Cloud Run service switches its DATABASE_URL secret to pablo-app-database-url; jobs needing owner keep pablo-database-url.
- With pablo_app non-owner and lacking UPDATE/DELETE on audit_logs, it genuinely cannot mutate or re-grant or DISABLE TRIGGER -> absolute immutability; the trigger remains as a complementary layer.
- Re-verify RLS/FORCE-RLS behaviour under the non-owner role; integration test that pablo_app cannot UPDATE/DELETE audit_logs even by attempting to arm the GUC.
Effort ~1-2 days + multi-env credential rollout.

title: Absolute audit-log immutability via DB role separation (follow-up to PABLO-5zy)

title: Bump redis-py 5→8 (PR #306) — verify retry_on_timeout still works
description:
Dependabot PR #306 bumps `redis` (the redis-py client) from 5.3.1 to 8.0.0 — three majors. Deferred pre-launch (06-08) for safety; revisit after.

## Audit of our call sites

We use redis-py in three places:
- `backend/app/redis_client.py` — single-instance sync client (Redis, ping, ConnectionError)
- `backend/app/rate_limit.py` — pipeline, zrem, scan_iter, delete
- `backend/app/services/auth_code_store.py` — pipeline, setex
- `backend/app/auth/idle_session.py` — exists, set, pipeline

All sync, single-instance, no async / cluster / pubsub / streams / sentinel — the surfaces that took the heaviest churn across 6/7/8.

## Likely papercut

`retry_on_timeout=True` is passed in `redis_client.py`. It was deprecated in 5.x in favor of a `retry=Retry(...)` object and may be silently dropped or warn in 8.x. Worst case: retry behavior disabled, not a crash. Verify and switch to the `retry=` form if needed.

## Plan when revisited

1. Check out PR #306 branch locally.
2. Install with poetry, confirm constructor accepts our kwargs without warnings.
3. Run rate_limit + auth_code_store + idle_session test suites against a real Redis container.
4. If clean, merge. If `retry_on_timeout` is gone, swap to `retry=Retry(ConnectionError, retries=3)` and amend the PR.

title: Implement Stage 3 LLM spot-check in source verification pipeline
description: source_verification_service.py documents a three-stage attribution pipeline: Stage 1 candidate retrieval (BM25 + embedding), Stage 2 hybrid signal-chain verification, Stage 3 LLM spot-check. Stage 3 is unimplemented and marked TODO at backend/app/services/source_verification_service.py:7 and :75, so source attributions currently rely on Stages 1 and 2 only. title: Audit Cloud Logging dual-write is synchronous on the request path
description:
AuditService._persist() mirrors every audit entry to Cloud Logging via audit_cloud_logging.write_to_cloud_logging(), which calls the low-level google.cloud.logging Logger.log_struct() — a synchronous write_entries() API round-trip. Because _persist runs inside the request handler (e.g. every patient view, session action, audio upload), each audited request pays a synchronous Cloud Logging round-trip (~tens of ms same-region) after the Postgres write.

It is best-effort (wrapped in try/except, so a mirror failure never fails the request), and the client build is one-time per process (@lru_cache on _gcp_logger), which is cheap on GCP where the metadata server is local. The remaining cost is the per-request synchronous mirror write on the hot path.

Improvement: move the mirror write off the request path — batched/background transport (e.g. BackgroundThreadTransport / the handler-based async logging path) or an outbound queue — so the canonical Postgres write is the only synchronous audit cost per request. Keep the best-effort, fail-open semantics. Postgres stays the audit-of-record; Cloud Logging stays the tamper-evident mirror.

Ref: backend/app/services/audit_cloud_logging.py (write_to_cloud_logging / _gcp_logger), backend/app/services/audit_service.py (_persist, audit_dual_write_enabled). Low priority: current cost is modest and bounded; revisit if audited-endpoint latency or audit volume grows.

title: Migrate e2e test runner off deprecated otplib 12 to otplib 13
description:
The e2e runner pins otplib 12.0.1, whose internal packages (@otplib/plugin-crypto, @otplib/preset-default, @otplib/plugin-thirty-two) are deprecated upstream in favor of otplib 13. This is a maintenance deprecation, not a vulnerability — npm audit on e2e/ is clean — hence low priority.

otplib 13 is a breaking API rewrite, not a drop-in bump:
- The authenticator singleton (.options / .generate()) used in e2e/fixtures/totp.ts is gone; v13 exposes functional generate()/verify() plus TOTP/HOTP classes.
- The package is ESM-first (type: module) with dual CJS exports.

Scope:
- Rewrite e2e/fixtures/totp.ts to the v13 API and bump otplib to ^13 in e2e/package.json.
- Confirm the three @otplib/* deprecation warnings are gone after the bump.

Acceptance (load-bearing): generated TOTP codes must stay RFC-6238 compatible (SHA1, 6 digits, 30s step) and keep satisfying the Firebase MFA enrollment + sign-in challenge. Verify by comparing v12 vs v13 output for a fixed secret/epoch, and by a green e2e run that exercises MFA.

Follow-up to the e2e Playwright suite work; no functional impact today.

title: Document-type tagging at upload time
description: Add a doc_type column to patient_documents with a defined enum (intake, lab, imaging, letter, prior_records, consent, other). Required field at upload (UI dropdown). Enables filtering, downstream auto-categorization (separate bead), and chart-UI grouping.

title: Bulk upload UI for multi-file intake batches
description: Frontend drag-drop / file-picker that accepts multiple files at once and creates a patient_documents row per file. Currently the upload UI is one-file-at-a-time. Common case: intake packet arrives as 5–10 PDFs that all attach to the same patient. Backend already supports concurrent uploads; this is purely a frontend UX change.

title: Auto-categorize uploaded documents by content
description: LLM-assisted classification of patient_documents into doc-type buckets (intake form, lab result, prior records, letter, image, other) based on extracted text. Pre-fills the doc-type field at upload; user can override. Reduces filing friction for the common case where a folder of scans needs sorting.

title: migration-lint flags doc-only model changes; refresh Icd10CodeRow docstring
description:
Two small follow-ups surfaced by PABLO-6xj.5 (pablo PR #380):

1. .claude/skills/migration-lint/check.py is purely file-level: any M to backend/app/db/{models,platform_models}.py demands a new alembic revision, even for docstring/comment-only edits with no schema change. This penalizes doc fixes to model files (you'd have to ship a no-op migration — slop — or skip the doc fix). Teach it to ignore changes that don't alter schema-relevant content (e.g. AST-compare ignoring docstrings/comments, or a sanctioned skip marker).

2. Deferred because of (1): Icd10CodeRow docstring in platform_models.py still says 'Seeded from app.diagnostics.baseline (a curated subset ...); a managed deployment may seed the full catalog.' After #380, codes are seeded from the bundled catalog (app.diagnostics.catalog, F01-F99 + Z55-Z65). Refresh the docstring to match — bundle it with the next PR that legitimately touches the model + a migration.
